reason: WP-1 governance PR #481 exact head fa6a6fc14d21834472f4e0174c33817f492fdd80 exposed a real cross-platform Layered CI trusted-Git acquisition defect. Windows job 95776404332 failed only because prepareGitDependencies returned null after its production git helper killed a multi-ref origin fetch at the hard-coded 15000ms timeout. The same runner's preceding checkout single-ref fetch took about 20071ms, while the exact-head Ubuntu layered governance matrix passed. The root fix belongs in the existing delegated-product L2 trusted-Git verifier: keep the strict 15000ms default for local Git identity operations but give the network fetch an explicit bounded 60000ms timeout, with a permanent regression proving the fetch-specific bound while preserving fail-closed semantics. No workflow, routing, authorization policy, product source, dependency or scanner change is authorized.

causalRed.failingTest: real historical delegated L2 V2 head fails closed when canonical base no longer equals its authorization merge
causalRed.failure: prepareGitDependencies returned null before semantic verification
rootCauseEvidence: tools/layered-ci/verify-delegated-product-l2.js hard-codes timeout: 15000 for every Git operation, including the multi-ref network fetch in prepareGitDependencies.
The same Windows runner's actions/checkout fetch of one SHA took approximately 20.071 seconds before this test executed.

The failing prepareGitDependencies fetch requests main, the preserved implementation branch, and the candidate SHA in one remote operation, so the 15-second production timeout is lower than an observed healthy Windows network fetch on the same runner.
All other 204 layered-ci tests passed in that Windows job and the same exact-head portable Ubuntu layered governance job passed.

digestCanonicalization.pathNormalization: Require exact repository-relative normalized paths, remove duplicates, then sort with JavaScript default Array.prototype.sort().
digestCanonicalization.canonicalText: Join the normalized sorted unique path list with LF and append exactly one trailing LF before hashing.

requiredBehavior: Preserve the existing trusted Git environment, exact branch/SHA validation, force fetch semantics, fail-closed null result and downstream trusted-main authority evaluation.
Keep 15000ms as the default timeout for local Git identity, show, rev-parse and diff operations.
Allow the existing git helper to accept an explicit per-operation timeout without introducing a new scheduler, retry subsystem or environment-driven policy.
Call only the prepareGitDependencies network fetch with an explicit 60000ms bounded timeout.
Add a permanent layered-ci regression that proves the fetch has the explicit larger timeout and the default local Git timeout remains 15000ms.
Do not rerun or retry inside production verification code; one bounded fetch either succeeds or fails closed.
forbiddenBehavior: No workflow runner change, no Windows exclusion and no matrix weakening.
No test skip, timeout-only test annotation change or same-head rerun used as the repair.
No removal of the historical real-Git regression.
No broad increase of every Git command timeout to hide unrelated hangs.

negativeProofs: No workflow, route, scanner, dependency or product source change.
No retry loop or unbounded network wait.
Historical real-Git fail-closed coverage remains active on Windows and Ubuntu.

reviewedCandidates.name: Existing delegated-product L2 trusted-Git verifier
reviewedCandidates.reason: The defect is a too-small network timeout in the existing authority; the correct fix is a narrow per-operation option in that verifier, not new infrastructure.

reviewedCandidates.name: Git native bounded fetch
reviewedCandidates.source: git fetch invoked through node:child_process execFileSync
reviewedCandidates.license: GPL-2.0-only for Git; Node built-in API
reviewedCandidates.reason: The existing implementation already uses native Git; an explicit bounded process timeout is sufficient and avoids custom retry/network code.

retireOrAvoid: Do not add retry/backoff infrastructure around Git fetch.
Do not weaken or skip the Windows layered-ci matrix.
Do not raise every Git operation timeout globally when only the network fetch requires a larger bound.
Do not convert the real-Git regression into a mocked-only test.
